```{r Chapter 1 Example}
# vote share base on economic growth
data(hibbs)
plot(hibbs$growth, hibbs$vote, xlab="Average Recent Growth in Personal Income", ylab = "Incumbent Party's Vote Share")

M1 <- stan_glm(vote ~ growth, data = hibbs)

abline(coef(M1), col="blue")

print(M1)

#comparing LM to Stan_glm
M2 <- lm(vote ~ growth, data = hibbs)

abline(coef(M2), col="red")

stargazer(M2, type = "text")
```

```{r}
data(hibbs)
plot(hibbs$growth, hibbs$vote, xlab="Economic growth",
ylab="Incumbent party's vote share")
M1 <- stan_glm(vote ~ growth, data = hibbs)
print(M1)
abline(coef(M1))
1 - pnorm(50, 52.3, 3.9)


#checking fit procedure using fake data simulaiton
a <- 46.3
b <- 3.0
sigma <- 3.9
x <- hibbs$growth
n <- length(x)

y <- a + b*x + rnorm(n, 0, sigma)
fake <- data.frame(x, y)


fit <- stan_glm(y ~ x, data=fake)
print(fit)

b_hat <- coef(fit)["x"]
b_se <- se(fit)["x"]

cover_68 <- abs(b - b_hat) < b_se
cover_95 <- abs(b - b_hat) < 2*b_se
cat(paste("68% coverage: ", cover_68, "\n"))
cat(paste("95% coverage: ", cover_95, "\n"))

n_fake <- 1000
cover_68 <- rep(NA, n_fake)
cover_95 <- rep(NA, n_fake)
for (s in 1:n_fake){
y <- a + b*x + rnorm(n, 0, sigma)
fake <- data.frame(x, y)
fit <- stan_glm(y ~ x, data=fake, refresh=0) # suppress output on console
b_hat <- coef(fit)["x"]
b_se <- se(fit)["x"]
cover_68[s] <- abs(b - b_hat) < b_se
cover_95[s] <- abs(b - b_hat) < 2*b_se
}
cat(paste("68% coverage: ", mean(cover_68), "\n"))
cat(paste("95% coverage: ", mean(cover_95), "\n"))
```










```{r Chapter 5: Simulation}
#sim for average heights
height_sim <- function(N){
  male <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.48)
  height <- ifelse(male==1, rnorm(N, 69.1, 2.9), rnorm(N, 63.7, 2.7))
  mean(height)
}

avg_height <- replicate(1000, height_sim(N=10))

hist(avg_height)

z <- rnorm(1e4, 5, 2)
cat(mean(z), median(z), sd(z), mad(z))
# MAD is median absolute deviation * 1.483 (used in special case of normal distribution) or hand calc as 1.483*median(abs(z - median(z)))


#bootstrapping example with earnings & gender data
data(earnings)
earn <- earnings$earn
male <- earnings$male
ratio <- median(earn[male==0])/median(earn[male==1])


boot_ratio <- function(data){
n <- nrow(earnings)
boot <- sample(n, replace = TRUE)
earn_boot <- earn[boot]
male_boot <- male[boot]
ratio_boot <- median(earn_boot[male_boot==0]) / median(earn_boot[male_boot==1])
}

n_sims <-10000
output <- replicate(n_sims, boot_ratio(data=earnings))
hist(output)
print(sd(output))


```

```{r LODES Data Setup}
library(lehdr)
options(lehdr_use_cache = TRUE)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)



rac <- grab_lodes(state = "mn", year = 2002:2023, lodes_type = "rac",
                  job_type = "JT01", segment = "S000",
                  agg_geo = "block", download_dir = "~/R Files/myrepo/Lodes",
                  use_cache = TRUE, geometry = TRUE)

xwalk <- grab_crosswalk("mn", download_dir = "~/R Files/myrepo/Lodes")

mcd <- rac %>%
  left_join(dplyr::select(xwalk, tabblk2020, ctycsub),
            by = c("h_geocode" = "tabblk2020")) %>%
  group_by(year, ctycsub) %>%
  summarise(across(c(C000, starts_with("CNS")), sum), .groups = "drop")

```


```{r Ch 9.1 - 9.2}
data(hibbs)
plot(hibbs$growth, hibbs$vote, xlab="Economic growth",
ylab="Incumbent party's vote share")
M1 <- stan_glm(vote ~ growth, data = hibbs)
print(M1)

sims <- as.matrix(M1)
Median <- apply(sims, 2, median)
MAD_SD <- apply(sims, 2, mad)
print(cbind(Median, MAD_SD))

a <- sims[,1]
b <- sims[,2]
z <- a/b
print(c(median(z), mad(z)))

new <- data.frame(growth=2.0)
y_point_pred <- predict(M1, newdata=new)

new <- 2.0
a_hat <- coef(M1)[1]
b_hat <- coef(M1)[2]
y_point_pred <- a_hat + b_hat*new

new <- data.frame(growth=2.0)
y_linpred <- posterior_linpred(M1, newdata=new)

sims <- as.matrix(M1)
a <- sims[,1]
b <- sims[,2]
y_linpred <- a + b*as.numeric(new)

y_pred <- posterior_predict(M1, newdata=new)
n_sims <- nrow(sims)
sigma <- sims[,3]
y_pred <- a + b*as.numeric(new) + rnorm(n_sims, 0, sigma)
hist(y_pred)

y_pred_median <- median(y_pred)
y_pred_mad <- mad(y_pred)
win_prob <- mean(y_pred > 50)
cat("Predicted Clinton percentage of 2-party vote: ", round(y_pred_median,1),
", with s.e. ", round(y_pred_mad, 1), "\nPr (Clinton win) = ", round(win_prob, 2),
sep="")

new_grid <- data.frame(growth=seq(-2.0, 4.0, 0.5))
y_point_pred_grid <- predict(M1, newdata=new_grid)
y_linpred_grid <- posterior_linpred(M1, newdata=new_grid)
y_pred_grid <- posterior_predict(M1, newdata=new_grid)

x_new <- rnorm(n_sims, 2.0, 0.3)
y_pred <- rnorm(n_sims, a + b*x_new, sigma)



data(earnings)
fit_1 <- stan_glm(weight ~ height, data=earnings)
print(fit_1)

earnings$c_height <- earnings$height - 66
fit_2 <- stan_glm(weight ~ c_height, data=earnings)
print(fit_2)

new <- data.frame(c_height=4.0)
y_point_pred_2 <- predict(fit_2, newdata=new)
y_linpred_2 <- posterior_linpred(fit_2, newdata=new)
y_postpred_2 <- posterior_predict(fit_2, newdata=new)
```

```{r Ch 9.3 - 9.5}
data(hibbs)
plot(hibbs$growth, hibbs$vote, xlab="Economic growth",
ylab="Incumbent party's vote share")
M1 <- stan_glm(vote ~ growth, data = hibbs)
abline(M1)
print(M1)

theta_hat_prior <- 0.524
se_prior <- 0.041
n <- 400
y <- 190
theta_hat_data <- y/n
se_data <- sqrt((y/n)*(1-y/n)/n)
theta_hat_bayes <- (theta_hat_prior/se_prior^2 + theta_hat_data/se_data^2) /
(1/se_prior^2 + 1/se_data^2)
se_bayes <- sqrt(1/(1/se_prior^2 + 1/se_data^2))
print(theta_hat_bayes)
print(se_bayes)

# 9.5
M3 <- stan_glm(vote ~ growth, data=hibbs,
prior_intercept=NULL, prior=NULL, prior_aux=NULL)
sims <- as.data.frame(M3)
a <- sims[,1]
b <- sims[,2]
plot(a, b)

prior_summary(M3)

M1 <- stan_glm(vote ~ growth, data=hibbs)
prior_summary(M1)

M4 <- stan_glm(vote ~ growth, data=hibbs, prior=normal(5, 5), prior_intercept=normal(50, 10))
print(M4)

x <- seq(-2,2,1)
y <- c(50, 44, 50, 47, 56)
sexratio <- data.frame(x, y)
lm_sexratio <- lm(y ~ x, data = sexratio)
fit_default <- stan_glm(y ~ x, data=sexratio)
print(fit_default)

fit_post <- stan_glm(y ~ x, data=sexratio,
prior=normal(0, 0.2), prior_intercept=normal(48.8, 0.5))
print(fit_post)
```
